# The EU-frames case {.unnumbered .unlisted}

::: {.home-lead}
This site teaches reproduction, robustness and replication in R on one published claim, together with the reanalyses that the claim received in a many-analyst study and the replication that tested it with new data. It is part of Applied Replication for Data Skills (AR4DS), which teaches the same exercise on four cases.
:::

::: {.home-cta}
[Formats](#formats) [Read the case study](cases/eu-frames/index.qmd)
:::

## The case {.unnumbered}

::: {.home-intro}
A sociological paper of 2016 asked, from the Eurobarometer surveys of the years 2004 to 2013, whether the economic crisis changed how citizens of the European Union frame the Union. One sentence of its abstract became the claim that the course works on.
:::

> "... poor economic performances ... decrease positive dimensions of EU framing" [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic, p. 619]

The case study tells the story in four parts: the original study, its data and the selections behind them, SCORE and Multi100, the five reanalysts, and the comparison of their results. The case teaches the aggregation of repeated cross-sections into a panel, fixed and random effects and the within–between model, inference with few clusters, and a multiverse of `r e_spec` specifications, on a panel of `r e_cells` country-years built from the Eurobarometer surveys and shipped with the workspace.

::: {.home-cta}
[Read the case study](cases/eu-frames/index.qmd)
:::

::::

:::: {.home-rs .home-reveal}

::: {.home-r}
### Reproduction {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Two attempts to reproduce the published result from the original materials did not succeed.
:::

::: {.home-r}
### Robustness {.unnumbered .unlisted}

All five Multi100 analysts concluded that the data support the claim, while the partial correlations recorded for their results run from `r e_r[1]` to `r e_r[2]`.
:::

::: {.home-r}
### Replication {.unnumbered .unlisted}

A replication on later Eurobarometer waves was judged not successful.
:::

## Formats {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

::: {.home-intro .home-reveal}
The facilitator of a course chooses its format, and the link that you receive for a course leads to it. Each format is an ordered route through the pages of this site, with a sidebar that lists its parts, a slides page, and links at the foot of every page to the part before and the part after. The one-day workshop works on the country-year panel alone, while the third day of the Extended course takes the respondents within it.
:::

:::: {.home-grid}

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [Short session](tracks/eu-frames-short/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[Two halves, with R inside the slides]{.home-meta}

Three hours on the claim and its five reanalyses, with nothing to install and nothing preregistered: the estimand statement, the reproduction of one recorded result, the specification menu with your own tries on the class chart, the curve of 864 and how to read it, and the replication with new data.
:::

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [One-day workshop](tracks/eu-frames-one-day/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[Four parts, mainly in the browser lab]{.home-meta}

The claim and the credibility of social science, with the record of the paper in SCORE, the estimand and the causal graph, the reproduction of one of the reanalyses that worked on country-years, chosen by each participant, and the robustness exercise: the specification menu, the class chart and its submissions, the curve of the claim, and one analysis declared before it runs.
:::

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [Extended course](tracks/eu-frames-extended/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[Three days, built around the workshop]{.home-meta}

A first day on open research and the tools, the same for every case, the workshop as the second day, and a third day on the methods of the case, from the panel to the respondents within it, which ends with a report of your own, written in Quarto and kept under Git.
:::

::: {.home-track .home-reveal}
### [Self-study](tracks/self-study/index.qmd) {.unnumbered .unlisted}

[At your own pace, in R]{.home-meta}

The case for a reader who works alone, in R on your own machine, with the modules of the [companion](companion/index.qmd) between the tasks of the exercise and a project of your own at the end.
:::

## The exercise {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

::: {.home-intro .home-reveal}
Every format works through the same five tasks: the one-day workshop, the Extended course, whose second day is the workshop, and the self-study route. The decisions that the tasks ask for fall into three groups: those about the question that the analysis answers, those about how the variables are measured, and those about the model, how it is fitted and how its uncertainty is judged.
:::

:::: {.home-reveal}

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 1</span>The setup check</summary>

Check that your tools work before the rest of the work depends on them: the setup check of the browser lab, or the check script of the workspace.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 2</span>The panel, the estimand and the graph</summary>

Meet the country-year panel, write the estimand statement behind the claim, and finish the causal graph that goes with it. The graph shows what the fixed effects of a country-year panel do and do not absorb.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 3</span>The reproduction</summary>

Choose one of the five analysts and reproduce the value that Multi100 recorded for that analyst, from the data behind it. Three of the five fitted their models on means of countries or of cells, and their results come back to the third decimal from files that the browser lab already holds, which is why the one-day workshop reproduces one of these three. The other two worked on respondents, whose files only a GESIS account can give.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 4</span>The menu</summary>

Work through the decisions that lie between the data and a result, try alternatives one change at a time, and send one exploration to the class chart. The [decision map](cases/eu-frames/map.qmd) lays every decision out.

</details>

<details>
<summary><span class="home-n">Task 5</span>Declaration and report</summary>

Declare one specification in a short preregistration, run it, report it, and find where it sits among the `r e_spec` specifications of the [curve of the claim](cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd).

</details>

::::

The [exercise overview](cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) sets out the five tasks in full.

:::::

:::::: {.home-section #about}

## The course {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

:::: {.home-reveal}

<details>
<summary>What the course teaches</summary>

The main aim of the course is to introduce technical skills for modern empirical data analysis: finding the data and code of a study in an online repository, working with code so that another person (or your future self) can reproduce your steps, fixing your analytical choices in a preregistration before you run the analysis, and writing a live report that combines code and text. The exercise follows the design of Multi100 on a smaller scale, with many analysts testing the same claim, each stating their analytical choices, and results reported in a form that allows them to be compared, and the [exercise overview](cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd) sets out its five tasks.

</details>

<details id="running-the-analyses">
<summary>Running the analyses</summary>

The exercise is done in R, either in the [browser lab](cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd), which runs R inside a browser tab with the data in the page and nothing installed, or in the workspace on your own machine, which the [setup page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html) on the AR4DS site installs in plain steps. The respondent files behind the panel come from the GESIS archive, under a free account and terms that do not allow them to be passed on, so the Extended course, whose third day works on the respondents, asks each participant to download [the Eurobarometer files](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-eurobarometer-files-for-the-individual-level-work) under an account of their own.

</details>

<details>
<summary>The companion</summary>

The [companion](companion/index.qmd) holds the teaching material of the course on this case, in three groups: tools, data and sharing, and methods. Every module keeps its own page and stands on its own, so you can read one for the skill that it covers or take it in the place that a format gives it. A single day has room for the exercise and very little else, which is why the workshop points to the modules rather than working through them, while the Extended course teaches some of them as sessions and the self-study route is built out of them.

</details>

<details>
<summary>SCORE and Multi100</summary>

The claim comes from the work of SCORE, a programme that put claims from published social and behavioural research through reproduction, robustness checks and replication, and the exercise follows the design of Multi100, its study of robustness. The AR4DS site describes [the programme and the record of the four cases of the course](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/score-multi100.html), and its page on [the Multi100 article](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/multi100-article.html) explains how the results of the analysts were placed on one scale and compared.

</details>

## Getting started {.unnumbered .home-reveal}

::: {.home-intro .home-reveal}
The one-day workshop is taught in the browser lab, with the installation of R, an IDE and the workspace as part of its preparation, and the Extended course and the self-study route work in the workspace from the start.
:::

:::: {.home-steps .home-reveal}

::: {.home-step}
### R and an IDE {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Install R, Quarto and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), following the steps for your operating system. [Install and check](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html)
:::

::: {.home-step}
### The workspace {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Download the workspace of the case as a zip file, open it in your IDE and run the check script. [The workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-workspace)
:::

::: {.home-step}
### The browser lab {.unnumbered .unlisted}

Try the exercise in the browser, without installing anything; it is also the fallback when a machine fails on the day. [Open the browser lab](cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd)
:::

## Chris Moreh {.unnumbered}

::: {.home-role}
Lecturer in Sociology, Newcastle University
:::

<!-- The biography is quoted from chrismoreh.com (source: D:/GitHub/chrismoreh-source/index.qmd), as CM asked on 2026-10-25. -->

A social scientist interested in the political sociology of migration, mobility, ethnicity and nationalism.

Hailing from Transylvania, trained in anthropology and sociology at [Eötvös Loránd University of Budapest](https://tatk.elte.hu/en/) and [Central European University](https://sociology.ceu.edu/), and with a PhD from [Northumbria University](https://www.northumbria.ac.uk/), I currently work as a Lecturer (Assistant Professor) in Sociology at [Newcastle University (UK)](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/gps/staff/profile/chrismoreh.html).

I approach social research as a comparative, interdisciplinary and multimethodological endeavour. My work has combined ethnographic observation, document analysis, survey methods and statistical modelling.

I'm enthusiastic about transparency and reproducibility in the social sciences, and my [pedagogical approach](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/mediav8/library/file-downloads/research-services/open-research/moreh.pdf) seeks to develop skills that facilitate open and credible research practices.

[chrismoreh.com](https://chrismoreh.com)
